title: One Uniswap pool is governed as three separate Grove Instances, making the Instance boundary a mandate rather than a contract
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.1.2.2.3, .12.2.2.2.3 and .12.3.2.2.3 all record the same Pool Address, `0xbAFeAd7c60Ea473758ED6c6021505E8BBd7e8E5d`, and the same two underlying asset addresses. The three Instances differ in *what Grove is authorized to do there*: swap only (deposit and withdrawal limits "N/A - swaps only"), provide liquidity (25,000,000 deposit cap, unlimited withdrawal), and the Grove Diamond PAU mandate (5,000,000 aggregate with slope 0, 100% CRR, 5,000,000 USDS exposure ceiling).

So the unit of governance is not the venue. An Instance is a *(venue, operation set, mandate)* triple, and one contract can host several of them.

The RateLimitIDs make this concrete and also show where the seams are. The Diamond PAU Instance's swap RateLimitIDs (`0x7dd93dac…` for AUSD, `0x6e850dcb…` for USDC, at A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.3.2.3.7–.8) are the *same hashes* used by the Swaps Instance at .12.1.2.3.1–.2; its deposit and withdrawal IDs are the same as the LP Instance's. The three Instances are therefore overlapping views onto a shared set of on-chain limit slots, not three isolated silos.

That has a consequence worth stating plainly: capacity consumed under one Instance's mandate can deplete the limit another Instance relies on, because they share the underlying rate-limit slot. The Atlas separates the mandates cleanly at the document level while the enforcement layer keeps them coupled — so the per-Instance caps read as independent budgets but do not behave as independent budgets.
description: The Swaps, LP and Diamond PAU Instances all point at pool 0xbAFe…8E5d but register distinct RateLimitIDs and caps, letting Grove throttle each activity on a single venue independently.
